title: ⭐⭐ Revision: gifts, types and a description

questions.prompt: Nour writes: "I can navigate that big website without any help." What does she mean?

options.text: that she builds a new page for a website
that she finds her way from page to page
that she sails across a very wide sea
that she teaches others how to use a computer

questions.explanation: "that she finds her way from page to page" is the meaning: to navigate is to find your way, and on the internet the sea becomes a set of pages. "that she sails across a very wide sea" is the older meaning, the one a sailor uses; a website is not water. "that she builds a new page for a website" would be to create, and "that she teaches others how to use a computer" would be to train somebody, neither of which is finding a way.

questions.prompt: Slim writes about a gifted neighbour: "He is nineteen, and he is tall and thin." The lesson asks for three kinds of information about the person. Which one is still missing?

options.text: his age
his physical appearance
his social background
his school results

questions.explanation: "his social background" is the one still missing: Slim gives nineteen, which is the age, and tall and thin, which is the appearance, but he says nothing about the family and the world his neighbour comes from — the father's trade, the street, the house. "his age" and "his physical appearance" are both already there in the sentence, and "his school results" is not one of the three the lesson asks for: this whole lesson refuses to measure a person by marks.

questions.prompt: Bilel writes an acrostic on the word PUPILS. His fourth line is: "I am one of the pupils in this class." Give the two reasons why that line is wrong.

options.text: it does not open with an -ing verb, and it is much longer than the other lines
it does not open with an -ing verb, and it writes the word the poem must hide
it starts with the wrong letter, and it is not a sentence
it starts with the wrong letter, and it writes the word the poem must hide

questions.explanation: "it does not open with an -ing verb, and it writes the word the poem must hide" is the pair of faults: the line opens with I am, a subject and a conjugated verb, where every line of the model poem opens with an -ing form, and it prints the word pupils, which an acrostic never does — the letters down the left already say it. The letter itself is right: PUPILS has I in fourth place, so blaming the letter is looking at the wrong thing. And an acrostic line is not meant to be a full sentence, so neither its length nor its sentence shape is a fault here.

questions.prompt: Amira understands a rule the first time it is explained to her. Which sentence says so in correct English?

options.text: Amira has gifted at understanding a new rule.
Amira is a gift at understanding a new rule.
Amira is a prodigy of understanding a new rule.
Amira is gifted at understanding a new rule.

questions.explanation: "Amira is gifted at understanding a new rule." is correct: gifted is an adjective, so it follows the verb to be, and it takes at before an activity. "Amira has gifted at understanding a new rule." uses that adjective as if it were a noun. "Amira is a gift at understanding a new rule." turns the girl into the ability itself, and "Amira is a prodigy of understanding a new rule." uses a word reserved for a very young person with an astonishing ability, with a preposition that does not follow it.

questions.prompt: Wassim gets average marks, but he can mend anything in the house and he explains each repair clearly to his little brother. A neighbour says he is not intelligent. What would the lesson answer him?

options.text: He will become intelligent when his marks improve.
School marks are the only real proof of intelligence.
There is more than one sort of intelligence, and mending is one of them.
Explaining things clearly to a child is not a sign of intelligence.

questions.explanation: "There is more than one sort of intelligence, and mending is one of them." is the lesson's whole reply: Wassim shows the mechanical type, and the neighbour is judging him on one type only. "School marks are the only real proof of intelligence." is the narrow definition the opening activity asks you to question. "He will become intelligent when his marks improve." keeps the same narrow measure, and "Explaining things clearly to a child is not a sign of intelligence." throws away a second sign, since making somebody else understand is itself a gift.

questions.prompt: You must organise everything you have collected into the description you are going to write. Which plan follows the lesson?

options.text: what he can do, an example of each, then age, looks and background
his age and his looks only, in one long paragraph
the list of the six types of intelligence, then his name
the poem first, then the questionnaire, then his name

questions.explanation: "what he can do, an example of each, then age, looks and background" is the plan: the statements you chose come first, each one carried by its example, and the three details close the portrait. "his age and his looks only, in one long paragraph" keeps the decoration and drops the subject. "the list of the six types of intelligence, then his name" copies the questionnaire instead of describing anybody, and "the poem first, then the questionnaire, then his name" lines up the activities of the lesson rather than the information they produced.
